payload.body: Graph workflow executions are static after launch: every context always runs, the graph shape is fixed at seed time (agent-side mutation is limited to task-adds within one context), and the only repetition the engine supports is the failure-driven implement/validate retry loop. D2 landed schema-validated structured outputs per context, but nothing consumes them for control flow — a captured classifier verdict cannot activate one branch and skip another, an agent cannot fan out N candidate contexts at runtime, and no construct expresses "repeat this work until a judge says it is done." As a result four of the six target workflow patterns (Classify-And-Act, Generate-And-Filter, Loop-Until-Done, and larger compositions of them) are inexpressible or require abusing the validation loop. This is D4 of the workflow-vision roadmap (ticket command-center#39, Phase 2): make the graph engine dynamic at runtime — conditional paths, runtime graph expansion, and general loops — without giving up deterministic scheduling, durable auditability, or the engine's safety invariants.
payload.title: Problem

payload.body: After D4, three dynamic capabilities are first-class in the graph engine and three workflow patterns become expressible as ordinary templates: (1) Conditional paths — an edge may carry a deterministic activation guard over its source context's captured D2 output, so a classifier context routes exactly the branches its verdict selects and untaken branches skip cleanly (Classify-And-Act). (2) Runtime graph expansion — an authorized running implementer appends a bounded subgraph (new contexts, tasks, edges, including edges into multiple pre-declared unstarted downstream consumers) through one idempotent command, so a generator fans out N candidate contexts converging on a planner-authored filter (Generate-And-Filter, dynamic fan-out). (3) General loops — a declared loop group repeats a single-entry/single-exit body of one or more contexts by cloning it into immutable per-pass instances until a designated exit context's captured output satisfies the exit predicate, with worker + independent-judge bodies working from the first slice (Loop-Until-Done). All control flow remains deterministic and engine-evaluated: agents supply judgment exclusively as typed structured outputs, and every routing, expansion, and loop decision is reconstructible from durable events.
payload.title: Outcomes

payload.body: Out of scope for D4: other roadmap deliverables (D3 specialist validators, D5 lightweight parallelism, D6 pattern proving ground, D7 ephemeral workflows, D8 orchestrating agent, D9 DSL); any fourth orchestration shape or new runtime; cycle edges in the scheduled graph; agent-evaluated edge conditions as a mechanism; reopening or resetting completed contexts; resurrecting skipped contexts or a reroute operation (deferred until evidence demands it); a completion-on-exhaustion loop mode (locked Q15: exhaustion halts, only); zero-task control-only contexts; nested or overlapping loop groups; runtime expansion from inside an active loop body; agent-declared loop groups; validator-initiated expansion or per-expansion human approval; doc 06 slice 5 structural-edit UI forms (deferral re-confirmed, Q18); plan-repair edits to loop body membership and all repair structural ops (repair triggering on loop_limit_reached, cap raise, and audited exit-predicate amendment ARE in scope per answered spec question Q1 and ask batch q_e0ea3807); a loop-scoped mutable store or message bus (the pass ledger is a derived projection over durable captures and events; free-form inter-pass context stays in the worktree and shared documents); changes to the worktree-per-lane cost model (D5's job — D4 accepts ~20.8s serial provisioning per fan-out sibling under caps).
payload.title: Non-goals

payload.body: Locked closeout bar (Q19): (1) the three pattern integration proofs (Classify-And-Act, Generate-And-Filter, worker+judge Loop-Until-Done) green as engine-level tests; (2) one durable live mini-execution per unlocked pattern, run against the real engine with real LLM lanes, completing and publishing; (3) the FULL repository suite green at the published tip (both D1 and D2 shipped past scoped batteries with repo-wide standing failures); (4) zero behavior change for pre-D4 templates and persisted executions — absent D4 fields parse under the additive floor, and execution exhibits observational equivalence per R14's named projections (scheduling decisions, context status transitions, typed event sequences, modulo timestamps and generated identifiers).
payload.title: Success measures

payload.body: All structural mutation — agent expansion and engine loop unrolling alike — rides applyLiveExecutionEdits inside executionRepository.mutateActive under the loop-generation fence and the live-edit frontier invariant, with server-derived sources; never a second mutation path, never a bare repository write. The Kahn acyclicity check stays authoritative and continues to re-run on every accepted live edit. The completed context status stays terminal. One pure shared control-flow projection module owns guard resolution, skip propagation, active-dependency selection, and publish settlement; the scheduler, lane readiness, joins, upstream-input resolution, completion, final publish, CLI, and UI all derive from it and never re-implement route semantics. Guard documents are validated and evaluated exclusively through the single-source schema-subset module (validateJsonSchemaSubset and its exported descriptor) — no second evaluator; the module is soundness-sensitive (own-property access, adversarial fixtures). New config defaults are seeded only in SEEDED_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS. Persisted-field discipline applies to every new field: repository mapping, maximal round-trip contract fixture (assertRoundTripDurability), migration/floor behavior, and blob-bounds declarations for blob-shaped fields. The task-completion loop and context validators stay first-class — loops are additive. Standard repo contract: red-green TDD, strict typing, no vi.mock for internal modules, typed event publication, bun run seams:check on boundary changes.
payload.title: Constraints

payload.body: Tier-1 product forks were locked by Alex via ask batches q_8dcdc0d5 (2026-08-01, 19 answers) and q_6c74033a (2026-08-02, 2 answers), on the negotiated design in memory-bank/collaboration/d4ed48bd-4671-438a-a1aa-60f0250d476f/round-1/agent_one/final_answer/answer.md. Divergences from the joint recommendation, all binding: Q10 — generated contexts MAY carry agent-supplied operational config overrides, narrowed 2026-08-03 (batch q_a57ccbe1) to a tuning ALLOWLIST — implementer, iterationPolicy, circuitBreaker, scriptValidator — after external review showed full overrides could disable child validators and approval gates; gate-weakening blocks (contextValidator, humanApprovalGate, askUserQuestions, collaboration, planRepair, mutability) stay cascade-owned, and expansion authority is force-disabled on children AFTER config inheritance, preserving sibling mutability fields; Q15 — loop exhaustion is a resumable loop_limit_reached halt ONLY (no completion opt-in); Q13 — worker+judge (multi-context) loop bodies are required from the first loop slice; Q8b — an expansion may feed MULTIPLE pre-declared rejoin targets (each individually downstream of the invoker, unstarted, and unreserved at apply time). Revision-2 locks (2026-08-03, review feedback + spec question Q1 + ask batch q_e0ea3807): loop_limit_reached JOINS the plan-repair trigger set; repair loop authority = raise maxPasses plus audited, non-retroactive exit-predicate amendment; inter-pass communication = an engine-derived pass ledger injected bounded into body prompts plus a documented handoff-field schema convention (no new mutable channel — locked; worktree files and shared documents remain available for free-form context); R2's route algebra is worded as uniform conjunctive edge satisfaction. Revision-3 changes (2026-08-03, first external review): R2 composes explicitly with the existing land-gate; the expansion envelope forbids payload tasks targeting any pre-existing context; the loop terminal contract is explicit; loop pass instances clone from a VERSIONED BODY TEMPLATE owned by the loop declaration — template content is the edit/repair target with per-pass version provenance (completed pass instances are never edited); resume after loop_limit_reached re-decides against the final pass's exit output under the current predicate/cap; the criterion-skip guard extends to every mutation path; R12 is a must; the enum-coverage lint is scoped to single top-level enum/const guards; pre-D4 compatibility is observational equivalence. Revision-4 changes (2026-08-03, second external review, Codex): the success-measures byte-identity language is corrected to match R14's observational-equivalence projections; fan-in/skip topology is stated explicitly (direct guards AND-compose on the target; skipped intermediates' unconditional edges are omitted) and an activated else counts toward cardinality; loop input pinning applies to loop-BOUNDARY inputs only (same-pass worker-to-judge injection is ordinary), and an untaken loop's silent skip is distinguished from an active loop's loop_exit_skipped halt; the total-pass backstop is concrete (25 per execution, scope "execution", constant, resumable, not raisable); the ledger records append-only predicate-versioned DECISION records so re-decisions after amendment coexist; the impossible-output halt names its remedy (quiescent live edit of the unstarted target's incoming edges, then resume); criterion protection uses a transitive MUST-RUN model with the compile-time check honestly marked vacuous until spec authoring can express routing and the delivery gate's proof floor as terminal backstop; ordinary CLI/UI structural edits are pinned to still require quiescence (expansion and loop unrolling are the only server-derived running exceptions); new events scope to conditional decisions only (pre-D4 event sequences unchanged) with authoritative durable decision records deriving the views. The reviewer's minimal-v1 scope cuts (defer cardinality/lint, loop templates + repair triggering, the pass ledger, multiple rejoins) were declined by Alex (batch q_a57ccbe1) — all prior locks stand. Key substrate anchors: edges are a flat {id, sourceContextId, targetContextId} triple (definition-schemas.ts:112-119); Kahn acyclicity re-runs on every live edit via the frontier (validation.ts:216, runtime-edits.ts:1696); completed is terminal (context-transitions.ts:87) and completed contexts are frozen against edits (runtime-edits.ts:704); structural ops exist but are quiescence-gated (runtime-edits.ts:1313); applyAddContext inherits config from configFromContextId/cascade (runtime-edits.ts:1388-1417); the output lookup is four-state captured|pending|orphaned|none (context-outputs.ts:34-44); context completion precedes commit/lane-visibility (iteration-orchestrator.ts, lane-readiness.ts:27) — why R2 must compose with the land-gate; the spec compiler emits only unconditional edges today (specs/compiler.ts:290); worktree provisioning is ~20.8s serial per fan-out lane (workflow-manager.ts:1610); the plan-repair allowlist excludes structural ops (plan-repair/schemas.ts:37-60). Expansion caps locked at 5 contexts/request, 10/adding context, 25/execution (Q12). The remaining Tier-2 technical-design forks (shared projection contract, live-edit/evidence freezing, idempotency/audit shapes, growth dimensions, rejoin proof, loop decision transaction, per-pass inheritance and ledger bounds, migration floor, naming) are locked during the design stage.
payload.title: Locked decisions and substrate

payload.statement: An execution-context edge shall optionally carry a source-local activation guard — either a D2 schema-subset document the source context's captured output must match, or an else marker — validated at accept time: a guard-bearing edge requires its source to declare an outputSchema, the guard document must itself satisfy the schema subset, and at most one else edge is admitted per source context.

payload.text: Accept-time validation (create, replace, edit, live edit, and expansion paths) refuses a guard-bearing edge whose source declares no outputSchema, a guard document outside the schema subset, and a second else edge on one source — each with a typed error naming the edge and JSON path.

Guard evaluation uses the shared schema-subset validator: a captured source output matching the guard document activates the edge and a non-matching output deactivates it, with pending/orphaned/none lookups never evaluating — proven at the projection level with adversarial fixtures (__proto__, constructor, exotic keys). (Durable recording of evaluations is covered by R13.3.)
At runtime an else edge activates exactly when no conditional sibling edge from the same source activated, independent of edge declaration order.

payload.statement: The engine shall resolve routes deterministically under one uniform rule: a context becomes eligible when every incoming edge is satisfied, where an unconditional edge is satisfied when its source lands (and is omitted when its source is skipped) and a conditional edge is satisfied when its guard evaluates true over the completed source's captured output — conditional edges are not a special veto class; all drawn edges are conjunctive prerequisites. Guard evaluation gates only the routing decision; target eligibility additionally honors the existing land-gate: a satisfied edge schedules its target only once the source's work is committed and lane-visible, and a source whose fan-in merge is pending or failed blocks (never skips) its dependents until the merge resolves or the execution halts. Guards resolve only after the source context completes; a guard whose source is skipped resolves false; a resolved-false guard skips the target; when every predecessor path is skipped, a fan-in skips recursively. A completed conditional source with an unevaluable output (pending, none, or orphaned) produces a typed resumable invariant halt whose sanctioned remedy is a quiescent live edit of the unstarted target's incoming edges (amend or remove the guard, or reroute), followed by resume — never a false evaluation, and never an edit to the completed source.

payload.text: A target with one landed unconditional dependency and one resolved-false conditional guard is skipped, not run — pinning the uniform rule that every drawn edge is a conjunctive prerequisite and a sibling edge's satisfaction cannot override an unsatisfied guard.

validationStrategy.note: the mixed-input counterexample from the design negotiation; the any-active alternative makes guards advisory in mixed shapes

payload.text: A conditional edge does not resolve while its source holds a captured output but is not completed (e.g. parked on a human approval gate); an approval rejection that deletes the capture leaves the route unresolved rather than latched.

Skip propagation and fan-in compose by topology: a fan-in whose incoming edges are unconditional but sourced from branch contexts (one skipped intermediate, one landed) runs on the landed branch with the skipped source's edge omitted; a target carrying a direct resolved-false guard skips regardless of its other satisfied edges (R2.1); when every predecessor path of a fan-in is skipped, the fan-in and its exclusive descendants skip recursively; the fan-in always waits for every incoming route to resolve first.

validationStrategy.note: pins the omitted-edge-from-skipped-intermediate topology that reconciles R2.1 with single-active-branch fan-ins

payload.text: A completed conditional source observed with a pending, none, or orphaned output lookup halts the execution with a typed resumable invariant halt.

validationStrategy.note: defense-in-depth: state should be unreachable under completion gating + frozen frontier

payload.statement: Outgoing conditional matches from one source shall be independent by default (zero, one, or many branches may activate), with an optional per-source cardinality policy (atLeastOne or exactlyOne) that turns under- or over-selection into a typed resumable routing halt; an activated else edge counts toward cardinality, so a source with an else edge always satisfies atLeastOne and violates exactlyOne only on multiple activations; an authoring warning fires when a closed-enum guard field leaves values uncovered with no else edge; first-match-wins ordering shall not exist.

payload.text: exactlyOne halts on zero and on multiple matches; atLeastOne halts on zero matches; both halts are typed, resumable, and record the evaluated verdicts.

When every conditional guard from a source tests only a single top-level enum or const field, authoring uncovered values with no else edge produces a warning naming the uncovered values; guards testing deeper paths, multiple fields, or non-enum forms produce no warning (analysis is deliberately limited to the simple case).

payload.statement: A skipped context shall be a first-class terminal, frozen status: it holds no lane, owes no task, validator, approval, or output debt, contributes no merge input, records the guard verdicts that skipped it, is exempt from the completion invariant and final-publish preconditions, and is irreversible within the execution — no transition leaves skipped and reset-context refuses it.

payload.text: An execution containing skipped contexts completes: skipped contexts are exempt from the unfinished-task completion invariant and the output-debt sweep, final publish proceeds without them, and the parked/resume/restart paths preserve persisted skip states.
The context transition table admits no exit from skipped, and reset-context refuses a skipped context with a typed error.
A context-skipped event carries the evaluated guard verdicts, and downstream prompt injection labels a skipped upstream as a branch not taken rather than omitting it silently.

payload.statement: Skipping a context shall never implicitly waive a linked spec acceptance criterion, using a transitive MUST-RUN model: a context is must-run iff it carries no direct conditional guard and is either an entry context or has at least one unconditional edge from a must-run predecessor. At compile time, a spec scope in which some acceptance criterion has no coverage on any must-run context shall be refused with a typed error naming the criterion (vacuously satisfied today — the spec compiler emits only unconditional edges — and load-bearing the moment authoring inputs can express routing). At runtime, routing is locked around criterion coverage in spec-linked executions: every mutation path (live edit, expansion, loop unrolling) shall refuse — at the shared frontier — a change that leaves any linked criterion without at least one must-run covering context. The delivery gate's per-criterion proof floor remains the terminal backstop: a skipped covering context simply never produces evidence, so unproven criteria still block delivery.

payload.text: The spec-to-workflow compiler refuses a scope where some criterion has no coverage on any must-run context (per the transitive definition), and accepts the same scope once the criterion gains coverage on a must-run context; with today's unconditional-only compiler output every compiled scope passes vacuously.

payload.statement: A running implementer lane whose context resolves mutability.allowAgentContextAdd true shall append a bounded subgraph — new contexts with tasks, and edges — through one idempotent agent-facing command applied via the fenced prepare/finalize mutation staging without pausing the execution: every accepted request creates at least one new context; every new context is reachable from the invoker; every task in the payload targets a batch-created context; every edge source is the invoker or a batch-created node; every edge target is a batch-created node or one of multiple pre-declared rejoin contexts each individually downstream of the invoker, unstarted, and unreserved at finalize time; full validation runs during prepare with an O(payload) fenced finalize that re-verifies the definition fingerprint, liveRevision, envelope invariants, and absence of a pending halt; all-or-nothing; one liveRevision bump on acceptance and none on refusal.

payload.text: An authorized running lane adds contexts, tasks, and edges in one atomic request; the scheduler picks the additions up on the next tick without pause/resume, and the batch bumps liveRevision exactly once with the mandatory live-edit event plus a typed expansion event.

Envelope violations — unauthorized lane, node unreachable from the invoker, a task targeting the invoker, a rejoin target, or any pre-existing context, edge sourced outside the invoker/batch, edge into a started or reserved context, any remove/update/move/reorder op — are refused fail-closed with no partial write and a typed refusal event.

Retrying a request with the same source context, requestId, and canonical payload hash replays the prior acceptance receipt with no duplicate mutation (acceptance receipts permanent within the cumulative cap); the same requestId with a different hash is refused while the refusal record is retained; an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated against current state (requestIds documented single-use); an accepted request that would create zero new contexts is refused.

validationStrategy.note: aligned with the D5 eviction contract — no identical-re-refusal promise

payload.text: One expansion feeds multiple pre-declared rejoin contexts when each satisfies the per-target conditions (downstream of invoker, unstarted, unreserved — re-checked inside the serialized mutation); a batch with any failing rejoin target is refused whole.

payload.statement: Expansion authority shall be a per-context cascaded mutability flag seeded default-off, exercisable only by the bound implementer, authenticated by a signed lane capability scoped to the execution, context, conversation, and implementer lane and re-verified inside the serialized mutation. Generated contexts may carry agent-authored prose, acceptance criteria, tasks, a subset-valid outputSchema, and tuning overrides — implementer, iterationPolicy, circuitBreaker, and scriptValidator, the last MONOTONIC (enable-only; an override or seed that would disable an inherited-enabled script validator is refused). Protected blocks — contextValidator, humanApprovalGate, askUserQuestions, collaboration, planRepair, mutability — derive from the INVOKER's resolved config regardless of configFromContextId and refuse payload overrides, so no expansion path weakens a child's validation or approval gates. Expansion authority shall resolve disabled on every generated child after config inheritance from any source, preserving sibling mutability fields; and a generated context with zero tasks shall be refused.

payload.text: allowAgentContextAdd resolves false on every generated child under each inheritance source — global tier enabled, workflow tier enabled, invoker context-local enabled, and configFromContextId pointing at an enabled context — while every sibling mutability field (e.g. allowAgentTaskAdd) is preserved exactly as inherited; pinned by contract tests covering all four sources.

validationStrategy.note: the blocking-catch carve-out from the design negotiation; disable-after-inherit must not clobber siblings

payload.text: Tuning overrides (implementer, iterationPolicy, circuitBreaker, scriptValidator-enable) apply to generated contexts; disabling an inherited-enabled scriptValidator via override OR via a configFromContextId seed is refused; protected-block overrides are refused and protected blocks ignore configFromContextId (invoker-derived), pinned by a laundering test seeding from a validator-disabled context; a zero-task generated context is refused; a request without a valid implementer-lane capability (wrong lane kind, wrong conversation, stale scope) is refused with no mutation.

payload.statement: Expansion shall be bounded and audited with exact ceilings: per request ≤5 contexts, ≤25 tasks, ≤40 edges, and ≤64 KB canonical payload; ≤10 contexts per adding context; a CUMULATIVE ≤25 expansion-created contexts per execution (seed contexts and loop-pass clones excluded). Refusals shall emit typed events and persist refusal receipts in a bounded ring of the 20 most recent per execution; an attempt whose refusal record has been evicted is re-validated as a new attempt against current state. Accepted expansions shall persist permanent receipts (initiator, rationale, added ids, payload hash) with node-level provenance, bounded by the cumulative cap; and the persistence blob-bounds contract shall declare every new field.

payload.text: Requests exceeding any cap are refused with a typed refusal event; accepted expansions persist receipts and provenance that survive repository reload, proven against real SQLite persistence.

payload.statement: A seed-authored loop group shall repeat a connected single-entry/single-exit body of one or more contexts — with worker + independent-judge (multi-context) bodies supported from the first slice — by uniform immutable DAG unrolling with POST-LAND settlement: when a pass's exit instance has landed (completed, committed, lane-visible) or resolved skipped, one fenced settlement transaction evaluates the until predicate against the banked exit output and either concludes the loop, materializes the next pass (cloned from the versioned body template with reserved collision-proof ids for contexts, tasks, and edges), or halts; the settlement decision is idempotent on its durable decision record, an unconcluded loop's exit holds all external edges unresolved so downstream work cannot become eligible in the landed-but-unsettled window, and a completed-but-uncommitted exit is reconciled on resume via a durable commit intent before settlement proceeds. The loop terminal contract is validated at accept time: the exit context must declare an outputSchema and the until predicate must be subset-valid and statically compatible with it. Loop-boundary inputs are pinned via a durable activation-time snapshot — each pass's entry receives the snapshot plus the bounded Loop History (boundary routing edges are consumed once by the first pass and never cloned) — while ordinary upstream-input injection between same-pass body contexts is unchanged. Skip semantics distinguish an untaken loop (skips entirely with its body, no halt) from an active loop whose exit resolves skipped (typed loop_exit_skipped halt) or unevaluable (typed invariant halt). The graph remains acyclic and no completed context is reopened.

payload.text: A two-context worker+judge body executes end-to-end: a false judge verdict clones pass k+1 (fresh conversations, prior exit output injected), a true judge verdict completes the loop, and downstream consumes the final pass's outputs.
Prior passes remain completed and frozen with distinct per-pass captured outputs; the working definition is acyclic after every unroll; no context status re-enters from completed.
Exit evaluation precedes the pass-limit check: a satisfying verdict on the final allowed pass completes the loop normally.

Settlement is one fenced transaction, idempotent on its decision record key (loopGroupId, pass, loopControlRevision, exit-capture identity): a crash or restart at any point — before commit, between land and settlement, or mid-tick — re-derives to a consistent state with no duplicate or missing pass; downstream contexts of the loop's external edges never become eligible while the loop is unconcluded; a completed exit with a pending commit intent is committed on resume before settlement; and a cap-only repair (maxPasses raise bumping loopControlRevision) makes resume re-decide against the final pass's banked output.

validationStrategy.note: restart fixtures across each window; the projection-gate and control-revision cases pinned individually

payload.statement: Every loop group shall declare a mandatory maxPasses; exhaustion with an unsatisfied predicate shall halt the execution with a resumable loop_limit_reached halt recording the final verdict and pass count (no completion-on-exhaustion mode); per-context iteration and failure budgets shall reset each pass; a false exit verdict is control flow — it shall not increment failure counters nor trip the circuit breaker; pass counts shall survive resume without reset. A per-execution total-pass backstop bounds all loops together: a hard constant of 25 total passes per execution, counting every started pass across all loop groups; reaching it halts with loop_limit_reached carrying scope "execution" (per-loop halts carry scope "loop"); the halt is resumable but the backstop is a constant — neither operators nor plan repair can raise it.

payload.text: Pass exhaustion with a false verdict halts resumable loop_limit_reached, recording the final verdict and pass count; resume does not reset the pass count.
Iteration and consecutive-failure budgets reset per pass, and false exit verdicts across mixed pass/fail sequences never increment failure counters or trip the breaker.

validationStrategy.note: counter behavior pinned across mixed sequences

payload.statement: V1 loop composition shall be conservative: loop groups are seed-authored only (expansion payloads may not declare them); bodies are non-nested, non-overlapping, connected single-entry/single-exit subgraphs with external incoming edges targeting the entry and external outgoing edges originating at the exit; conditional branches inside a body must reconverge at the exit; runtime expansion from inside an active body is refused. Pass instances clone from a versioned body template owned by the loop declaration: template membership (which contexts form the body, entry, exit) freezes once the first pass starts; template content (context prose, acceptance criteria, and tasks) is editable only while the execution is paused or halted, each edit bumping the template version, and every pass records the template version it cloned; completed pass instances are never edited. The exit predicate is amendable only while the execution is halted (operator live edit or plan repair, each with a required rationale); raising maxPasses is the only other edit admitted on a started loop.

payload.text: Validation refuses nested or overlapping bodies, disconnected or multi-entry/multi-exit bodies, external edges bypassing entry/exit, non-reconverging conditional branches inside a body, loop declarations in expansion payloads, and expansion requests from a context inside an active body.

After the first pass starts: template-membership edits are refused; template-content edits are refused while running, accepted while paused or halted with the template version bumped, and appear in the next pass's clone with the cloned version recorded on the pass; edits addressed at completed pass instances are refused; exit-predicate amendments are refused while running and accepted with a required rationale while halted; raising maxPasses is accepted and takes effect on the next decision.

payload.statement: The D1 plan-repair supervisor shall trigger on loop_limit_reached halts in addition to its existing triggers, and its op allowlist shall admit loop repairs at three grains: raising a loop's maxPasses; amending a loop's exit predicate — with a required rationale recorded in an audit log, applied only at halt quiescence, and never retroactive (completed passes keep the verdicts they ran under); and editing the versioned body template's content (context prose, acceptance criteria, and task ops addressed at template tasks), which reaches subsequent passes through the normal clone-from-template path. Repair operations touching template membership and all structural ops shall remain refused fail-closed. Resuming from a loop_limit_reached halt re-runs the loop decision against the final completed pass's recorded exit output under the current predicate and cap: satisfied completes the loop, unsatisfied with budget starts the next pass, unsatisfied without budget re-halts — so a predicate-only repair takes effect at the resume decision even without a cap raise.

payload.text: The repair supervisor fires on a loop_limit_reached halt; repair ops raising maxPasses, amending the exit predicate, and editing template content validate and apply through the live-edit core; repair ops touching template membership or any structural op are refused fail-closed.

payload.statement: D4 shall ship full read-side legibility with structural writes remaining CLI-only: the graph page and inspector render conditional edges with their guards, skipped nodes with recorded reasons, loop groups with pass badges and budgets, and runtime-added nodes with provenance; the CLI live outline reports the same. Every D4 CONDITIONAL decision — guarded-edge resolution, skip, cardinality halt, expansion acceptance and refusal, loop decision — persists an authoritative durable decision record (typed events and execution state) from which UI and CLI views derive; unconditional-edge scheduling emits no new events, so pre-D4 executions' event sequences are unchanged.

payload.text: Component tests cover the new render states: guard chips on conditional edges, ghosted skipped nodes with reasons, loop pass badges with budgets, and provenance badges on runtime-added nodes.
The live outline reports edge guards, skip states with reasons, loop pass counters and budgets, and expansion provenance rows.

payload.statement: D4 shall be additive and dormant-by-default: definitions and persisted executions absent D4 fields shall parse as unconditional edges, no loops, and expansion disabled, and shall execute with observational equivalence to pre-D4 behavior — identical scheduling decisions, context status transitions, and typed event sequences modulo timestamps and generated identifiers; and every new persisted field shall be covered by its repository mapping, the maximal round-trip contract fixtures, migration/floor behavior, and blob-bounds declarations.

payload.text: Pre-D4 definition and execution fixtures parse with the additive floor semantics and execute with observational equivalence — the scheduling-decision, status-transition, and typed-event projections match pre-D4 recordings modulo timestamps and generated identifiers.

Every field in the authoritative persisted-field inventory — edge ids/guards, routing cardinality, loopGroups templates with resolved planRepair, skipReason, landingIntent with mode-specific receipts, routeSettlements, routeControlRevisions, loopStates (activation, slotLedger, loopControlRevision, boundaryInputs, latest decision markers), expansionReceipts — round-trips through the maximal contract fixtures against real SQLite, with blob-shaped fields declared in the blob-bounds contract and no superseded field (commitStatus, in-blob decision arrays) present in the schema.

payload.statement: Each unlocked pattern shall be proven by an engine-level integration test that authors and executes a real template — Classify-And-Act (classifier routes one branch, others skip, execution publishes), Generate-And-Filter (authorized generator expands candidates rejoining a pre-declared filter), and worker+judge Loop-Until-Done (exit within budget in one scenario, loop_limit_reached halt in another) — with a durable live mini-execution per pattern at closeout.

payload.text: A Classify-And-Act integration test executes: the classifier's captured output activates exactly one branch, sibling branches skip, the fan-in runs on the taken branch, and the execution completes and publishes.

validationStrategy.note: plus a live mini-execution at closeout per locked Q19

payload.text: A Generate-And-Filter integration test executes: an authorized generator expands N candidate contexts rejoining a pre-declared filter, the filter runs consuming all candidate outputs, and the execution completes and publishes.

validationStrategy.note: plus a live mini-execution at closeout per locked Q19

payload.text: A worker+judge Loop-Until-Done integration test executes both terminals: exit on a satisfying judge verdict within budget, and a resumable loop_limit_reached halt on exhaustion.

validationStrategy.note: plus a live mini-execution at closeout per locked Q19

payload.text: A predicate amendment without a rationale is refused; an accepted amendment records its rationale and is non-retroactive — prior passes retain their recorded verdicts; resume after loop_limit_reached re-decides against the final pass's recorded exit output under the current predicate and cap (a predicate-only repair therefore takes effect at the resume decision); a template-content repair appears in the next pass's clone with the template version recorded.

payload.statement: The engine shall maintain a per-loop ledger with bounded current state and complete durable history: the execution record retains bounded markers — activation state, pass count and reservations, the boundary-input snapshot, and the latest authoritative LoopDecisionRecord per pass (carrying the full deduplication key: loop, pass, loopControlRevision, exit-capture identity, template version, verdict, outcome) — while the complete decision history, including repeated re-decisions of one pass under amended control revisions, is durably recorded in the append-only event log; inspector and CLI ledger views derive from both. A bounded Loop History section (most-recent-N passes, size-capped) is injected into each pass's ENTRY prompt only; same-pass body contexts receive ordinary upstream injection. The ledger introduces no new mutable state and no new communication channel; free-form inter-pass narrative is schema-carried via a documented handoff-field convention for body outputSchemas in the planner skill.

payload.text: Pass k+1's ENTRY prompt contains the Loop History section — prior passes' per-body-context captured outputs, exit verdicts, and decision outcomes with their loopControlRevision — honoring the recency and size bounds; same-pass body contexts receive no history section and rely on ordinary upstream injection.

The full ledger — including multiple LoopDecisionRecords for a pass re-decided under different loopControlRevisions — is readable from the inspector and CLI via the shared cursor-paginated event reader combined with the blob's latest markers, and derives identically after a server restart.

A conditional target does not become eligible while its completed source's work is uncommitted or not lane-visible, and a source with a pending or failed fan-in merge blocks its dependents (existing merge-retry and halt semantics) rather than activating or skipping them.

validationStrategy.note: land-gate composition: guard truth is necessary but not sufficient for scheduling

payload.text: Accept-time validation refuses a loop whose exit context declares no outputSchema or whose until predicate is subset-invalid or statically incompatible with the exit schema, alongside the v1 body-shape refusals. (Runtime terminal behavior is covered by R9.6; entry-input injection by R16.1.)

In a spec-linked execution, a live edit or expansion that would leave a linked criterion without any must-run covering context — including making the last must-run covering context skippable via a conditional ancestor — is refused at the frontier with a typed error; the same mutation is accepted in an unlinked execution.

The 25-total-pass execution backstop halts a runaway loop independently of per-loop maxPasses with a resumable loop_limit_reached halt carrying scope "execution"; a repair or live-edit op attempting to raise the backstop is refused; context validators and human gates run on every pass exactly as on ordinary contexts.

After a server restart, every guarded-edge resolution, skip, expansion acceptance and refusal, and loop decision remains readable from its authoritative durable records, and the UI/CLI views derive from those records alone; a pre-D4 execution emits no new event kinds.

The running-time structural exception is exactly two server-derived paths — lane-agent expansion and engine loop unrolling; ordinary CLI and UI structural edits (add-context, remove-context, add-edge, remove-edge) still require a quiescent execution and are refused while running, pinned by tests on both surfaces.

validationStrategy.note: the narrow exception to the pause-only structural gate, named and fenced

payload.chosenApproach: Projection-resolved edges carry BOTH ids: logicalSourceId (the authored source — for a loop's external edges, the declared exitContextId) and effectiveSourceId (the context instance whose landed work and capture actually satisfy the edge — the concluding pass's exit instance for concluded loops; null while unresolved). The design names the consumer migration explicitly, because every current consumer reads edge.sourceContextId raw: the scheduler's prerequisite map, lane visibility (isUpstreamVisibleToDownstream and reachable-lane math), join source-lane planning, and upstream-input/prompt resolution all switch to projection-resolved edges and MUST use effectiveSourceId for landing, visibility, and data; UI/CLI render the logical id with the effective id as provenance. A lint (arch test) forbids new direct reads of edge.sourceContextId outside the projection and the validation module. Layered output lookup, loop-exit gating, and activation-aware resolution are unchanged from revision 7.
payload.reason: The logical exit stays immutable in authored topology while every runtime consumer is pointed, checkably, at the instance that really satisfies the edge.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Logical mapping without an effective-source contract
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Consumers reading edge.sourceContextId would wait on the never-running declared exit or merge the wrong lane — the round-5 blocker; the mapping only works if consumers are told which id to use for what.

payload.title: Projection exports logical and effective edge sources; every consumer migrates to projection-resolved edges

payload.chosenApproach: COMPATIBILITY: launching or loading a legacy definition with absent or duplicate edge ids does not refuse — ids are normalized deterministically with the existing mintLiveEdgeId scheme (src__tgt, then -2, -3 by duplicate ordinal) at inflate time, identically on every load, and saved-tier writes persist the normalized ids; uniqueness is enforced for NEW authoring. BUMP SET (closed list): a source's routeControlRevision bumps on add-edge, update-edge, or remove-edge touching any of its outgoing conditional edges (including else edges), a change to its routing.cardinality, an expansion adding a guarded edge from it, and a template edit altering guarded edges inside a loop body it sources. Nothing else bumps it. Guard wrapper, subset evaluation, compatibility lint, and id-addressed edits are unchanged from revision 7.
payload.reason: Identity becomes strict for new work without breaking old work, and the revision that keys settlement has a testably complete trigger list.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Refusing legacy definitions with duplicate edge ids
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Uniqueness must not brick existing templates at launch — normalization at the inflate boundary is deterministic and invisible. The round-5 compatibility gap.

rejectedAlternatives.label: An open-ended bump condition
rejectedAlternatives.reason: An unenumerated bump set cannot be tested for completeness; the closed list is pinned by tests.

payload.title: Legacy edge ids normalize deterministically; the routeControlRevision bump set is closed; guard design unchanged

payload.chosenApproach: Add "skipped" to graphWorkflowContextStatusSchema and CONTEXT_STATUS_TRANSITIONS (pending → skipped, ready → skipped; skipped → [] terminal); transitions happen only via transitionContextStatus inside the scheduling mutation, with the evaluated guard verdicts persisted as contextState.skipReason { edgeEvaluations: [{edgeId, verdict}], at } and a graph-workflow-context-skipped event. Exemptions wired through the projection: findContextsWithUnfinishedTasks, the output-debt sweep (contextOwesOutput loop), planFinalPublishJoin, getEligibleContextIds, and join source-lane math all treat skipped as settled-with-nothing. getContextOutput gains a fifth lookup kind { kind: "skipped" }; buildUpstreamInputsSection renders skipped predecessors as 'branch not taken'. resetContextStateToInitial throws on skipped (irreversibility lock).
payload.reason: R4's ripple has a dozen named consumers; a real status plus one projection is the only shape where a missed consumer is a compile/test failure rather than a stranded frontier.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Derived skip (no persisted status)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The skip is a durable routing decision with an audit obligation; deriving it per tick loses the terminal commitment, the reason record, and the event.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Flag on contextState beside status
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Status is the engine's lingua franca — every consumer switches on it; a parallel flag doubles every check.

payload.title: skipped as a first-class terminal context status with persisted reason

payload.chosenApproach: The execution blob retains only BOUNDED current markers: routeSettlements (≤ one per source, keyed by routeControlRevision), loopStates with the latest LoopDecisionRecord per pass plus counters/reservations, receipts within their caps. The FULL decision ledger — every route resolution, skip, expansion acceptance/refusal, and every loop decision including repeated re-decisions of one pass under amended control revisions — lives in the graph_workflow_events table, which is already append-only, unbounded by design, and durable; UI/CLI ledger views read events for history and the blob for current state. This resolves the contradiction where append-only decision arrays in the blob were not actually bounded by the 25-pass cap (one pass can be amended and re-decided repeatedly). Halt variants and event kinds are unchanged from revision 6; every event payload embeds the same record types the blob uses (LoopDecisionRecord, route settlement record).
payload.reason: Current state stays small and provably bounded; history stays complete where history already lives.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Append-only decision arrays in the execution blob
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Re-decisions under repeated amendments are unbounded while the blob claims bounds — the re-review's contradiction; events are the system's existing unbounded durable log.

payload.title: Bounded current markers in the blob; the full decision ledger lives in the events table

payload.chosenApproach: FENCE: the repository owns a monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit (scheduler and runtime mutations included — liveRevision alone misses them). prepareLiveExecutionEdits captures it with the snapshot; finalizePreparedEdits splices the prepared whole-state ONLY when the stateRevision is unchanged; otherwise it re-applies the prepared OPS payload-locally onto the CURRENT execution with the cheap envelope recheck (validation evidence carries over from prepare; a frontier-relevant conflict triggers a full reprepare outside the lock). Concurrent scheduler/runtime writes can therefore never be erased by an install. CAPS: the 25-context execution cap is CUMULATIVE over expansion-created contexts — seed contexts and loop-pass clones are excluded (loop clones are governed by the pass backstop) — so removal never frees budget and the cap is monotone. EVICTION: an unknown (requestId, hash) — including one evicted from the refusal ring — is treated as a NEW attempt and re-validated from scratch; the design drops the unkeepable promise of identical re-refusal, and requestIds are documented single-use (reuse with a different payload after eviction is indistinguishable from a new request and is validated as one). Capability auth, ≥1-new-context admission, canonical hashing, deterministic ids, permanent acceptance receipts unchanged.
payload.reason: The staging seam is safe under concurrency by construction, and every cap and idempotency promise is one persistence can actually keep.

rejectedAlternatives.label: liveRevision as the finalize fence
rejectedAlternatives.reason: liveRevision bumps only on live edits; scheduler/runtime mutations would be silently overwritten by installing a prepared execution. The round-5 blocker.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Guaranteed identical re-refusal after eviction
rejectedAlternatives.reason: State legitimately changes; the honest contract is re-validation-as-new, which is also what a correct retry wants.

payload.title: Prepare/finalize fenced by a repository-owned state revision; caps cumulative; eviction treated honestly

payload.chosenApproach: The compiler splits config into two classes. PROTECTED blocks {contextValidator, humanApprovalGate, askUserQuestions, collaboration, planRepair, mutability} always derive from the INVOKER's resolved config — configFromContextId cannot influence them (otherwise pointing at a validator-disabled context would launder a weakening through seeding). TUNING blocks {implementer, iterationPolicy, circuitBreaker, scriptValidator} seed from configFromContextId (else the invoker) and accept payload overrides — with scriptValidator MONOTONIC: an override may enable it (or set it enabled when inherited-off) but an override or seed that would turn an inherited-enabled scriptValidator off is refused, so no override path weakens validation. After composition, mutability.allowAgentContextAdd is stamped false, touching only that key. Contract tests cover the four inheritance sources, the seeding-laundering case, and the monotonic refusal.
payload.reason: Preserves Alex's tuning-yes/gate-weakening-no lock with the two holes the review found closed: monotonic script validation and invoker-anchored protection.

rejectedAlternatives.label: scriptValidator freely overridable
rejectedAlternatives.reason: enabled:false is expressible in the schema — a child could ship without script validation, contradicting R7's no-weakening intent. The design review's third blocker.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Protected blocks seedable from configFromContextId
rejectedAlternatives.reason: An agent-selected weaker seed context bypasses the denylist without any payload override — protection must anchor to the invoker.

payload.title: Child config: protected blocks derive from the invoker; scriptValidator override is enable-only

payload.chosenApproach: The backstop protocol is a durable slotLedger in loopStates: entries {pass, state: reserved | counted | released}. PASS 1 reserves its slot in the same mutation that marks the loop active (external activation resolved) — before any pass-1 instance becomes eligible; later passes reserve inside their settlement transaction before cloning, exactly as revision 7. Arbitration is durable and deterministic: within one scheduling mutation, loop groups are processed in definition order and the ledger records the grant order, so a restart replays identical arbitration; when no slot remains, activation or settlement halts scope execution without materializing. Provisioning failure releases the reservation durably and routes through the existing provisioning-failure halt path with the materialized pass instances halted-recoverable (resume retries provisioning and re-reserves; released slots are reusable). Logical exit mapping, activation states, boundary-input snapshot, reserved id patterns, and first-running counting are unchanged.
payload.reason: Every pass — including the first — is admitted through one durable, ordered, restart-replayable protocol.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Reservation only at settlement (pass 1 unreserved)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Pass 1 was admitted outside the protocol — a graph with many loops could activate more pass-1s than the backstop permits. The round-5 gap.

rejectedAlternatives.label: In-memory arbitration order
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Serialized settlements do not imply definition order across ticks and restarts; only a durable grant ledger replays identically.

payload.title: Durable slot ledger with definition-order arbitration; pass 1 reserves at activation; provisioning failures release and halt recoverably

payload.chosenApproach: The landingIntent is persisted when the context is DISPATCHED — the same mutation that assigns its lane records { baselineSha (the lane head at assignment, currently runner-local preTurnLaneHeadSha), laneId, worktreePath, mode, token, state: pending } — so no landing evidence ever exists only in memory. Modes carry mode-specific replayable evidence: lane_commit and solo_commit embed the deterministic token in the commit message (reconciliation probes the branch for token/SHA); fan_in_merge reconciles against the join's own durable merge records; approval-gated contexts keep the intent pending until approval resolves, then land normally. Reconciliation runs at resume/normalization and marks intents landed or retry; route and loop settlement treat only landed as satisfied. The remainder of settlement is unchanged from revision 7: projection-gated eligibility, LoopDecisionRecord as the idempotent done-marker keyed (loopGroupId, pass, loopControlRevision, exitCaptureIteration), prepare/finalize staging, resume re-decision under amended control revisions.
payload.reason: Every landing mode leaves durable, replayable evidence from before the first turn, so restart classification never guesses.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Intent persisted at finalize
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The baseline lives only in the runner until finalize — a crash mid-turn or a self-committing lane loses the baseline the reconciler needs; dispatch-time persistence closes it. The round-5 blocker.

rejectedAlternatives.label: One universal token for all modes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Fan-in merges and approval flows do not produce a single token-bearing commit; mode-specific evidence is what each landing path actually leaves behind.

payload.title: Landing lifecycle: mode-specific intent persisted at dispatch; settlement waits on reconciled landings

payload.chosenApproach: History access gets a real reader: a shared cursor-paginated events reader (seq-keyed, ascending or descending, bounded page size) over the graph_workflow_events table, used by the inspector ledger view, the CLI ledger/outline surfaces, and tests — the existing events endpoint exposes only a bounded tail, which cannot serve full decision history. Current state comes from the blob markers (loopStates, routeSettlements, receipts). Loop History prompt injection is ENTRY-ONLY, bounded (3 passes / 2 KB per context / 16 KB per section), sourced from the blob markers and pass-instance captures — never from the paginated reader (prompts need recent, not full, history). The handoff-field outputSchema convention is documented in the planner skill in the same change.
payload.reason: Complete history is reachable through one shared reader while prompts and reducers keep reading bounded current state.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Serving history from the bounded event tail
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A long execution's early decisions fall off the tail — full history needs pagination. The round-5 gap.

payload.title: Ledger views read blob markers plus a shared cursor-paginated event reader

payload.chosenApproach: Because the resolved working definition intentionally drops workflow-tier config, the loop repair policy is resolved AT SEED into each loop group: loopGroups[].planRepair (cascade workflow → global at resolve time, exactly like per-context blocks), persisted on the working definition — so the policy source survives in the artifact the engine actually reads. Repair accounting keys on loopGroupId with attempts-per-loop-group semantics; planRepairRounds entries carry loopGroupId. The op set is unchanged (raise-loop-max-passes, amend-loop-predicate with rationale, loop-template content ops; structural and backstop ops unrepresentable) with one addition to semantics: every accepted loop-control op bumps loopControlRevision, which is what makes the subsequent resume re-decide (see the settlement decision). Backstop halts: cap-raise refused, predicate/template amendment + resume re-settlement remain the remedy.
payload.reason: R12 with a policy source that exists in the persisted artifact and op semantics that provably unblock re-decision.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Workflow-tier policy read at repair time
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The resolved definition does not retain workflow-tier blocks — the policy would be unreadable at the moment it is needed. The re-review's gap, closed by seed-time resolution.

payload.title: Loop repair policy resolved per-group at seed; ops bump loopControlRevision

payload.chosenApproach: The route projection exports the inductive must-run set (no direct guard AND (entry OR ≥1 unconditional edge from a must-run predecessor)). The spec compiler's refusal (vacuously satisfied today — it emits only unconditional edges) and the runtime lock both consume it: checkLiveEditFrontier gains a check, active only for spec-linked executions, that every linked criterion retains ≥1 must-run covering context after the batch; the criterion→context coverage map is supplied by the specs domain through the registered GraphExecutionContract port (no direct import — the existing seam). The delivery gate's per-criterion proof floor remains the terminal backstop and needs no change: skipped coverage simply never produces evidence.
payload.reason: R5's transitive model with one computation site and enforcement on the path every mutation already rides.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Direct-guard-only 'unconditional context' check
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Unsound — a conditional ancestor skips transitively; the second review's counterexample.

rejectedAlternatives.label: specs domain imports workflow-graph internals
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Violates the canonical boundary; the contract port exists precisely for spec-side policy injection.

payload.title: Criterion protection: must-run computed in the projection, enforced at the frontier via the contract port

payload.chosenApproach: This decision IS the inventory; R14.2 mirrors it and the persisted-blob-bounds contract test enumerates exactly these fields. DEFINITION TIER: edges[].id (required unique; legacy definitions normalized deterministically at load), edges[].when, contexts[].routing (cardinality), loopGroups[] (template with contexts/tasks/internal edges, entry/exit ids, until, maxPasses, resolved planRepair block, templateVersion). RUNTIME TIER: contextStates[].skipReason; contextStates[].landingIntent { baselineSha, laneId, worktreePath, mode: lane_commit | fan_in_merge | solo_commit, token, state: pending | landed | retry, receipts } persisted at DISPATCH (before the first agent turn); execution.routeSettlements[sourceContextId] { captureIteration, routeControlRevision, evaluations, cardinalityOutcome, at } (≤1 per source); execution.routeControlRevisions[sourceContextId] (monotonic); execution.loopStates[loopGroupId] { activation: pending | active | untaken | concluded, passCount, slotLedger: [{pass, state: reserved | counted | released}], loopControlRevision, boundaryInputs snapshot, latest LoopDecisionRecord per pass }; execution.expansionReceipts { accepted: permanent within the cumulative cap, refusals: 20-entry ring }. REMOVED/SUPERSEDED: the boolean commitStatus (landingIntent replaces it) and any append-only decision arrays in the blob (the events table holds full history; the blob holds latest markers only). All fields Zod-optional with floor defaults; one additive migration; repository mapping + codec + maximal round-trip fixtures + blob-bounds declarations for template, receipts, boundaryInputs, skipReason, landingIntent, and loopStates; storage.ts accept-time validation covers new authored fields.
payload.reason: Persistence has exactly one authoritative declaration site, mirrored by the contract tests.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Partial per-decision field listings
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Revision 7 left D12 naming superseded fields (commitStatus, in-blob decisions) while newer decisions introduced landingIntent and the event ledger — the review's staleness blocker; one inventory decision ends the drift class.

payload.title: The authoritative persisted-field inventory (supersedes every earlier partial listing)

payload.chosenApproach: derive-graph.ts adds edge guard presence/verdict, skip state with reason, loop-group membership with pass badges (pass K of maxPasses), and provenance badges for runtime-added nodes; ExecutionContextNode renders guard chips (dashed conditional edges) and ghosted skipped nodes; ExecutionInspectorPanel gains guard, skip-reason, loop (ledger view), and expansion-provenance sections; live-outline.ts adds guard/skip/loop/provenance rows and cctl workflow live get renders them. All new UI states covered by component tests with Storybook-free fixtures (testing rules); StatusChip tones for skipped. Doc 06 slice 5 (structural-write forms) remains deferred per Q18.
payload.reason: R13's legibility bar with the smallest new-surface area: extend the exact components and outline that D2 extended.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Structural-edit UI forms now
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Deferred by Alex (Q18): the vocabulary should stabilize before forms fossilize it; D4's structural writers are agents via CLI.

payload.title: Read surfaces: derive-graph + inspector + live outline extensions, no structural forms

payload.chosenApproach: A test harness runs pre-D4 fixture definitions through the engine with deterministic fake agents and records three named projections — scheduling decisions (which contexts became eligible/dispatched in what order), context status transition sequences, and typed event kind sequences — normalized modulo timestamps and generated ids. The recordings are committed as fixtures; the D4-enabled engine must reproduce them exactly. Parse-floor tests cover absent-field defaults on both tiers. This replaces any byte-identity claim.
payload.reason: R14's named projections made mechanically checkable and regression-pinned.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Byte-identical assertions
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Impossible alongside defaulted new fields — the contradiction the second review caught; observational equivalence is the meaningful guarantee.

payload.title: Compatibility proven by recorded observational-equivalence projections

payload.body:
Shape: three author-facing concepts (edge `when` guards, `cctl workflow graph expand`, `loopGroups`) over shared internals — the D2 subset evaluator, the pure route projection over a dependency-free raw output lookup, and the fenced mutation core reached through three typed entry points riding one prepare/finalize staging seam fenced by the repository-owned executionStateRevision (bumped on every commit; splice only when unchanged, payload-local re-apply otherwise, reprepare on frontier conflicts).

Persisted boundaries (the authoritative inventory lives in the persistence decision): ROUTING — routeSettlements keyed (source, captureIteration, routeControlRevision) with a closed, tested bump set; legacy edge ids normalize deterministically at inflate. LOOPS — loopStates with activation states, the durable slotLedger (pass 1 reserves at activation; definition-order grants; provisioning failures release and halt recoverably), loopControlRevision, boundary-input snapshot, and latest LoopDecisionRecords. LANDING — mode-specific landingIntent persisted at dispatch with replayable evidence per mode (commit token, join records, approval records); settlement waits on reconciled landings. IDENTITY — reserved clone id patterns refused in authored plans. HISTORY — latest markers in the blob; complete history via the shared cursor-paginated event reader.

Loops route downstream through the logical exit with an explicit two-id contract: consumers use effectiveSourceId (the concluding pass's exit instance) for landing, visibility, and data, and logicalSourceId for topology and rendering; an arch lint forbids raw edge.sourceContextId reads outside the projection and validation. Untaken loops resolve as skipped sources.

Expansion: capability auth, staged prepare/finalize, ≥1-new-context admission, CUMULATIVE 25-context cap excluding seed and loop clones, permanent acceptance receipts, ring-bounded refusals with eviction treated as new-attempt re-validation (requestIds documented single-use).

Implementation slices and naming as previously locked, plus executionStateRevision, slotLedger, landingIntent modes, effectiveSourceId/logicalSourceId, and the paginated ledger reader.

Proof obligations: settlement idempotence across crash windows including post-git-pre-persist landings per landing mode; prepare/finalize under concurrent scheduler mutations (stateRevision fence); slot arbitration replay across restarts; the A→B→A settlement case; consumer-migration lint; four-source + laundering child-config tests; route-settlement exact-once under repeated all-active ticks; observational-equivalence recordings for pre-D4 fixtures; legacy edge-id normalization determinism.
payload.title: Design narrative

payload.instructions: The terminal task — depends on every implementation, proof, surface, and docs leaf. Run the three live mini-executions against the real engine with real LLM lanes (author each pattern as a real template, launch via the normal start path, verify completion and publication against durable state per the cc-live-feature-test discipline); run the FULL repository suite (bun run test — not the changed-tests pre-merge subset) plus bun run typecheck, lint, and seams:check at the published tip; re-assert the observational-equivalence recordings and the restart decision-record replay across routing, expansion, and loop decisions (R13.3). Fix or surface anything red before claiming completion; this context runs with scriptValidator enabled.
payload.title: Closeout verification: live pattern proofs, full suite, equivalence hold

payload.instructions: Failing tests first for each refusal. Add `when: { schema } | { else: true }` to graphWorkflowContextEdgeSchema and `routing: { cardinality }` to the context definition (both tiers, Zod-optional). Extend validateWorkflowDefinition: guard-bearing edges require source outputSchema; guard documents pass validateOutputSchemaDeclaration plus the subset-descriptor compatibility walk; at most one else edge per source; edge ids required unique for NEW authoring with deterministic mintLiveEdgeId-style normalization of legacy definitions at inflate. Add id-addressed update-edge and `when`-bearing add-edge ops to both edit vocabularies (operator surface, quiescence-gated, unstarted-target rule; ambiguous endpoint remove-edge refuses listing candidates). Persist per-source routeControlRevisions with the closed bump set pinned by a completeness test. This task begins the runtime-edits.ts mutation-seam sequence — T7 and T6 build on it in order, never concurrently.
payload.title: Edge guards, edge identity, and the guard edit surface

payload.instructions: Two steps, one coherent module boundary. FIRST extract the raw four-state output lookup from context-outputs.ts into dependency-free output-lookup.ts (characterization tests pin behavior; context-outputs re-exports its public API byte-compatibly; existing tests stay green unmodified). THEN build route-projection.ts over it: per-edge resolution with guard evaluation via validateJsonSchemaSubset (matching activates, non-matching deactivates, non-captured lookups never evaluate — adversarial fixtures for __proto__/constructor/exotic keys), order-free else resolution, cardinality outcomes, the uniform conjunctive readiness rule, recursive skip derivation, the transitive must-run set, publish settlement, logical/effective loop-exit resolution (activation-state aware), and projection-resolved edges carrying logicalSourceId + effectiveSourceId. Unit-test the full truth table red-green including the mixed-input counterexample and the skipped-intermediate fan-in topology. Pure, browser-safe.
payload.title: Extract the output lookup and build the pure route-projection module

payload.instructions: Failing transition-table tests first. Add "skipped" to graphWorkflowContextStatusSchema and CONTEXT_STATUS_TRANSITIONS (pending → skipped, ready → skipped, skipped terminal); transitions only via transitionContextStatus with contextState.skipReason persisted in the same mutation and the graph-workflow-context-skipped event emitted. resetContextStateToInitial throws on skipped. getContextOutput gains the fifth public lookup kind { kind: "skipped" } composed in context-outputs (not the raw lookup); buildUpstreamInputsSection renders skipped predecessors as branch-not-taken. Repository mapping + round-trip fixture updates for skipReason ride along.
payload.title: The skipped context status lifecycle

payload.instructions: Engine integration under red-green: wire the route projection into getEligibleContextIds, classifyContextSchedulability, join planning, the completion invariant, and final-publish quiescence; migrate every consumer of edge.sourceContextId to projection-resolved edges (effectiveSourceId for landing/visibility/data) with the arch lint. Persist landingIntent at dispatch with mode-specific evidence and THE ACTUAL COMMITTERS integrated: the server-side lane committer (lane-committer.ts) and solo committer embed the deterministic token; self-authored lane commits adopted at head-advance gain verifiable evidence via the recorded baseline→head SHA range in the intent receipts; fan-in merges reconcile against join records. Reconciliation at resume/normalization; route settlement waits on landed intents (merge-pending/failed blocks, never skips). Write routeSettlements exact-once keyed (source, captureIteration, routeControlRevision) with the route-resolved event in the same mutation; add the routing_cardinality and routing_invariant halt variants with the quiescent edge-edit remedy proven. Prove skip ripple end-to-end: executions with skipped contexts complete, final publish excludes them, restart preserves persisted skips.
payload.title: Wire routing into the scheduler: settlements, landing intents, halts, and the consumer migration

payload.instructions: Failing tests first. Implement the scoped enum-coverage authoring warning (single top-level enum/const guards only). Export the transitive must-run set from the projection and consume it in two locks: the spec-to-workflow compiler refuses scopes where a criterion has no must-run coverage (vacuously satisfied today — assert explicitly), and checkLiveEditFrontier refuses — only in spec-linked executions via the GraphExecutionContract port — mutations leaving a linked criterion without a must-run covering context; the same mutation accepted in unlinked executions. Runs third in the runtime-edits.ts mutation-seam sequence, after the staging-seam split lands.
payload.title: Enum-coverage warning, must-run computation, and the criterion-skip locks

payload.instructions: Red-green at the repository seam. Add the repository-owned monotonic executionStateRevision bumped by EVERY mutateActive commit. Split the pure live-edit core into prepareLiveExecutionEdits (clone, apply, full frontier validation outside any lock) and finalizePreparedEdits (O(payload) under the fence: splice on unchanged stateRevision, payload-local re-apply otherwise, reprepare signal on frontier conflicts, refusal under pendingHaltReason). Prove the fence with interleaving tests: scheduler and runtime mutations between prepare and finalize are never erased; existing live-edit behavior unchanged. Runs second in the runtime-edits.ts mutation-seam sequence after the guard-schema task.
payload.title: executionStateRevision and the prepare/finalize mutation staging seam

payload.instructions: Failing route/service tests first. Own the capability chain END-TO-END: mint the signed implementer-lane capability at dispatch and inject it into the lane environment (the lane env builder in the task-run dispatch path), thread it through cctl workflow graph expand (env pickup, request header), and verify signature + scope at the route with the in-lock recheck that the conversation is the context's current implementer conversation. Implement the expansion service on the prepare/finalize seam: handle→deterministic-id compilation, the envelope (invoker running + flag, reachability, batch-only task targets, edge sources invoker/batch, targets batch or multi-rejoin re-checked at finalize, no remove/update/move/reorder, ≥1 new context), source lane-agent, one liveRevision bump on acceptance. Pin that CLI/UI structural ops still require quiescence.

payload.instructions: Failing validation tests first for every refusal. Add loopGroups to both definition tiers (body template with contexts/tasks/internal edges, entry/exit ids, until, maxPasses, templateVersion, seed-resolved planRepair block). The accept-time resolver snapshots authored body contexts into the versioned template, removes them from executionContexts, and materializes pass 1 with reserved ids (<loopGroupId>__p<K>__… for contexts, tasks, AND edges; authored ids matching the reserved pattern refuse). Terminal-contract validation: exit declares outputSchema, until subset-valid and statically compatible. payload.text: At runtime: a loop group whose external activation path is untaken skips entirely with its body and no halt; an ACTIVE loop whose exit resolves skipped halts with the typed loop_exit_skipped halt; an active exit with an unevaluable output produces the typed invariant halt; and each pass's entry receives the boundary-input snapshot plus the prior exit output through the loop-aware input resolver.

The prepare/finalize staging seam is fenced by the repository-owned executionStateRevision bumped on every mutateActive commit: a scheduler or runtime mutation interleaved between prepare and finalize is never erased — finalize splices only on an unchanged revision, re-applies ops payload-locally otherwise, and signals reprepare on frontier-relevant conflicts; finalize refuses under a pendingHaltReason.
